goblet-squat.description: A front-held dumbbell squat that trains the quadriceps while encouraging an upright torso.
instructions: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart and hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest.
Bend your knees and hips together, lowering between your legs while keeping the dumbbell close.
Press through your whole feet to stand tall and bring your hips beneath your shoulders.
Keep your heels planted and guide your knees in the same direction as your toes throughout.

dumbbell-squat.description: A squat performed with dumbbells at the sides for direct quadriceps and lower-body work.
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and set your feet in a comfortable squat stance.
Lower by bending your knees and hips, letting the dumbbells travel straight beside your legs.
Drive the floor away to return to standing, finishing with balanced pressure through both feet.
Keep your chest steady and prevent the dumbbells from pulling your shoulders or knees out of position.

barbell-back-squat.description: A barbell squat with the bar supported across the upper back, emphasizing the quadriceps and total lower body.
instructions: Set the bar across your upper back, grip it firmly, step clear of the rack, and establish your stance.
Brace your trunk and descend by bending your hips and knees while keeping the bar over midfoot.
Push through both feet to rise, extending your knees and hips together before resetting your breath.
Maintain a stable bar position and track your knees over your toes without letting your heels lift.

barbell-front-squat.description: A front-rack squat that places the bar ahead of the torso and strongly challenges the quadriceps.
instructions: Rest the bar across the fronts of your shoulders, lift your elbows, and stand with feet securely planted.
Sit down between your legs under control while keeping your elbows high and the bar stacked over midfoot.
Drive upward through your feet and finish tall without dropping your elbows as you pass the midpoint.
Keep the bar supported by your shoulders rather than your hands, and stop the descent before your rack position collapses.

smith-machine-squat.description: A guided-bar squat that provides a fixed bar path for focused quadriceps training.
instructions: Position the Smith bar across your upper back, place your feet under the intended bar path, and release the hooks.
Lower smoothly by bending your knees and hips while the bar follows the machine's vertical track.
Press through your feet to extend your legs, stand tall, and rotate the bar back onto the hooks when finished.
Confirm both hooks are clear before each repetition and fully engaged before stepping away.

hack-squat.description: A machine squat with back support and a guided sled, designed to emphasize knee extension and the quadriceps.
instructions: Place your back and shoulders firmly against the pads, set both feet on the platform, and release the stops.
Bend your knees to lower the sled under control while keeping your hips and back against the support.
Push the platform away until you return to the start, then reengage the safety stops after the set.
Keep your knees aligned with your toes and avoid forcefully snapping them straight at the top.

leg-press.description: A supported machine press that trains both legs together through a controlled knee-and-hip bend.
instructions: Sit with your hips and back against the pads and place both feet evenly on the press platform.
Release the carriage and bend your knees toward your torso without allowing your hips to curl off the seat.
Press the platform away through both feet and return the carriage to the secure stops after the final repetition.
Track your knees over your toes and keep them softly extended rather than locked at the top.

single-leg-press.description: A unilateral leg press that isolates each side while the seat supports the torso.
instructions: Set one foot securely on the platform and keep your hips square and your back in full contact with the pad.
Lower the carriage by bending the working knee toward your torso in a smooth, centered path.
Press through the working foot to return, complete the side, and switch legs without changing the seat setup.
Do not let the working knee collapse inward or the opposite side of your pelvis lift from the pad.

leg-extension.description: A seated machine exercise that isolates the quadriceps by extending the knees against the shin pad.
instructions: Adjust the seat so your knees align with the machine pivot and place the roller above your ankles.
Extend both knees smoothly to raise the pad until your legs are nearly straight.
Pause with the quadriceps engaged, then lower the pad under control to the bent-knee start.
Keep your hips against the seat and avoid kicking or rebounding the roller between repetitions.

bulgarian-split-squat.description: A rear-foot-elevated split squat that concentrates the work on the front quadriceps and glute.
instructions: Stand in front of a bench, rest the top of one foot behind you, and hold dumbbells at your sides.
Lower your rear knee toward the floor as the front knee bends, keeping most of your pressure on the front foot.
Push through the front foot to return to the split stance, then complete the side before switching legs.
Choose a stance that keeps the front heel down and prevents the elevated foot from twisting on the bench.

split-squat.description: A stationary staggered-stance squat that develops each quadriceps independently without stepping between repetitions.
instructions: Take a stable split stance with both feet pointing forward and your rear heel lifted.
Lower straight down by bending both knees while keeping your weight centered over the front foot.
Press through the front foot to rise back to the same split stance, then repeat before changing sides.
Keep your front knee tracking over its toes and avoid narrowing your stance until balance is lost.

forward-lunge.description: A stepping lunge that loads the lead quadriceps as the body moves forward and down.
instructions: Stand tall with feet under your hips and enough clear floor in front of you for one deliberate step.
Step forward, plant the whole lead foot, and bend both knees to lower your body under control.
Push firmly through the lead foot to travel back to the starting stance, then alternate or repeat the side.
Place the lead foot wide enough for balance and keep its knee aligned rather than drifting inward.

reverse-lunge.description: A backward-stepping lunge that keeps the front leg planted while training its quadriceps.
instructions: Stand upright with feet under your hips and brace before moving one foot behind you.
Step back onto the ball of that foot and lower the rear knee as the stationary front knee bends.
Drive through the front foot to bring the rear leg forward and finish in the original standing position.
Keep the front heel grounded and use a straight backward step that leaves enough width for balance.

walking-lunge.description: A traveling lunge that alternates legs and links repeated quadriceps-dominant steps.
instructions: Stand at the start of a clear path with your torso upright and feet facing forward.
Step ahead and lower through both knees until you reach a controlled lunge position.
Push through the front foot, bring the rear leg forward into the next step, and continue alternating sides.
Keep each step wide enough side to side for balance and prevent either knee from folding inward.

step-up.description: A forward platform ascent that uses one leg to raise the body and emphasize the quadriceps.
instructions: Face a stable platform and place one entire foot on top with the knee aligned over the toes.
Drive through the elevated foot to lift your body onto the platform without springing from the trailing leg.
Stand fully on the working leg, then step down with control and complete the side before switching.
Keep the working heel planted and verify the platform cannot slide or tip before beginning.

kettlebell-goblet-squat.description: A goblet squat using a kettlebell at the chest to train the quadriceps with a compact front hold.
instructions: Hold the kettlebell by the horns at your chest and set your feet in a balanced squat stance.
Lower between your legs by bending your knees and hips while keeping the bell close to your torso.
Press through your whole feet to stand and finish with the kettlebell still centered at chest height.
Keep your wrists neutral, heels down, and knees moving in line with your toes.

box-jump.description: An explosive jump from the floor to a raised platform that develops lower-body power led by the quadriceps.
instructions: Face a stable box with feet about hip-width apart and leave enough room for a natural arm swing.
Dip through your hips and knees, swing your arms, and jump upward and forward onto the box.
Land softly with both feet fully supported, stand to control the landing, and step down carefully.
Use a box you can clear without tucking excessively, and never jump down into the next repetition.

lateral-box-step-up.description: A sideways step-up that challenges the quadriceps while requiring control in the frontal plane.
instructions: Stand beside a stable box and place the nearer foot fully on top with your hips facing forward.
Press through the elevated foot to raise your body sideways while keeping the working knee aligned.
Reach a balanced stand on the box, then lower the outside foot to the floor with control before repeating.
Keep the elevated heel planted and avoid pushing off aggressively with the foot on the floor.

trx-squat.description: A suspension-assisted squat that uses the straps for balance while the legs perform the movement.
instructions: Face the anchor, hold a handle in each hand, and step back until the straps are lightly tensioned.
Bend your knees and hips to sit down between your feet while your arms remain long and relaxed.
Push through your feet to stand, using the handles only as much as needed to stay balanced.
Keep steady strap tension and do not lean back or pull yourself upward with your arms.

romanian-deadlift.description: A barbell hip hinge that lengthens and loads the hamstrings while the knees remain softly bent.
instructions: Stand with the bar at your thighs, hands outside your legs, and knees slightly bent.
Push your hips backward and lower the bar close along your legs while keeping your spine steady.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall, bringing the bar back to your thighs without leaning behind it.
Stop the descent when your hinge ends rather than reaching lower by rounding your back.

dumbbell-romanian-deadlift.description: A dumbbell hip hinge that targets the hamstrings with independent weights beside the legs.
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs and soften your knees.
Send your hips backward as the dumbbells slide close to your thighs and shins under control.
Press your feet down and bring your hips forward to return to a tall standing position.
Keep the dumbbells close and end the lowering phase before your back begins to round.

single-leg-romanian-deadlift.description: A one-leg dumbbell hinge that trains the hamstrings while challenging hip and trunk stability.
instructions: Stand on one softly bent leg with a dumbbell in the opposite hand and square your hips forward.
Reach the free leg behind you as you hinge, lowering the dumbbell near the standing leg in a controlled arc.
Drive through the standing foot and bring your torso and free leg back to the upright start.
Keep both hip points facing the floor and use nearby support if balance disrupts the hinge path.

seated-leg-curl.description: A seated machine curl that trains the hamstrings by bending the knees against a lower-leg pad.
instructions: Align your knees with the machine pivot and secure the thigh and ankle pads against your legs.
Curl the lower pad down and back by bending your knees while keeping your thighs pinned.
Pause at the curled position, then let the pad return slowly until your knees are extended comfortably.
Keep your hips against the seat and avoid lifting the thigh restraint or bouncing at either end.

lying-leg-curl.description: A prone machine curl that isolates the hamstrings as the heels travel toward the back of the thighs.
instructions: Lie face down with your knees near the machine pivot and the roller resting above your heels.
Bend your knees to curl the roller toward your thighs while keeping your hips against the pad.
Hold the top briefly, then lower your legs smoothly until they return to the starting position.
Keep your pelvis quiet and avoid arching your lower back to lift the roller farther.

standing-single-leg-curl.description: A standing machine curl that isolates one hamstring while the opposite leg provides support.
instructions: Align the working knee with the machine pivot, place the roller above its heel, and hold the supports.
Curl the working heel upward by bending only that knee while keeping both thighs parallel.
Pause at the top, lower the roller under control, and complete the side before changing legs.
Keep your hips square and avoid swinging your thigh or leaning your torso to move the pad.

nordic-hamstring-curl.description: A kneeling bodyweight exercise that challenges the hamstrings as they resist the torso falling forward.
instructions: Kneel on padding with your ankles firmly secured and hold a straight line from knees through shoulders.
Lower your body forward as one unit, resisting the fall with your hamstrings for as long as you can control it.
Catch yourself with your hands, press lightly from the floor, and use your hamstrings to return upright.
Keep your hips extended and place your hands ready to prevent an uncontrolled impact with the floor.
